discovery: Quantum key distribution and entanglement-based quantum cryptography

nominees.name: Charles H. Bennett
nominees.affiliation: IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center, USA

nominees.name: Artur Ekert
nominees.affiliation: University of Oxford, UK and Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore

motivation: Bennett and Brassard (BB84) showed that the laws of quantum physics (no-cloning and measurement disturbance) can guarantee the secrecy of a shared key, and Bennett and colleagues went on to demonstrate it experimentally. Ekert (1991) linked cryptographic security directly to Bell-inequality violation, turning a foundational test of quantum mechanics into a working resource. Bennett and Brassard also co-invented quantum teleportation (1993). Together these ideas founded quantum communication. They inspired loophole-free Bell tests, device-independent protocols, entanglement distribution over fibre and satellite links, and today's efforts to build a quantum internet. The work is rare in being both profoundly foundational and technologically transformative. It changed how physicists understand information as a physical quantity and started a field now pursued in laboratories and industry worldwide.
